# mdpdf

mdpdf turns Markdown files into PDFs from the command line. You can share, print or archive the output as-is. It doesn't need a browser engine or a LaTeX install, and setup is short.

It's written in Go and ships as a single 8 MB binary. Download it, put it somewhere on your `PATH`, and you're set. With no dependencies, it behaves the same on a laptop, in CI or in a small container image.

On speed, 100 pages render in about 1.2 seconds. That's fast enough for big documentation sets, generated reports, or a build step you don't want to wait on. You can regenerate documents as often as you like.

If you already write in Markdown and want PDFs without a heavy toolchain, mdpdf is easy to script and drops into the tools you already use.
